limitations: Browser visual and interaction acceptance remains blocked by the tool permission policy.

The benchmark uses one test account, eight fixed warmed queries and synthetic documents with copied real fixture vectors. It does not represent 50 distinct user profiles, cold arbitrary queries or production semantic relevance.
The fixed 19-query relevance set checks entity/name/alias regression only. Production relevance and online recommendation lift remain unproven.
Text and feature lag were measured independently from query load.
Synthetic model lifecycle tests do not satisfy the production training gate or justify rollout to real users. Online control was restored to the baseline.
The same-host Python threaded client is retained as a separate comparison, including its CPU cost. Its results are not mixed with the native HTTP measurements or treated as interchangeable.
Earlier d1d9877 and early held-corpus measurements did not verify embedding-worker liveness; the launcher issue is fixed and the latest run checks all isolated roles.

roleIsolation.note: Small-fixture diagnosis, not a substitute for the full benchmark. Timing headers were removed from final source.
changes: Search skips unused recommendation context reads; final user checks remain per request.
Independent lightweight recommendation workers avoid duplicating search encoders.
Model registry and its initial database connection are prepared during API startup.
Content-vector averaging uses the standard library without first-request NumPy imports.
Concurrent identical cold query encodings recheck cache after a bounded wait.
Isolated Kafka heap reduced from fixed 1 GiB to 256–512 MiB.

latestChanges: Cache hits and in-flight identical index queries share a completed/pending future without consuming recall executor slots.
Only cache misses are submitted to the bounded executor; independent cold channels remain parallel.
Executor rejection, queued cancellation and loader failure release pending entries and permit a fresh retry.
The local launcher restores the embedding switch after starting a recommendation role, including failed launches.
Server request IDs use UUIDv7 for time-local primary-key inserts, retaining legacy attribution and synchronous durable commits.
Four lightweight recommendation workers; search remains one process, with fifty Java database connections and unchanged request deadlines.
Java and Python failures record only operation/status/error class and elapsed time, without request data.

requestIds.limitation: Database counters cover the whole instance, including background workers. The UUIDv7 sample followed a Java restart; it demonstrates fewer observed physical reads, not a controlled end-to-end latency improvement.
requestIds.compatibility: Existing UUIDv4 requests retain attribution and ownership checks. No schema migration or asynchronous persistence; timestamps are not used as an authorization credential.

heldCorpus.earlyDiagnosticLimitation: The embedding worker was discovered inactive before fullroles-pool128 and then restored; early rounds are diagnostic, not full-stack acceptance.
heldCorpus.note: All repetitions are retained, including failed rounds. They were separate diagnostics before the final startup/caching fix.

gcExperiment.reason: Reduced observed GC pauses did not consistently lower P95. Final code retains normal garbage collection.
